tells.1: Too polished and aphoristic: the 'didn't feel triumphant so much as quietly astonished' contrast, the 'somehow the kindest thing' hedge, and the tidy closing room-in-my-house metaphor.
tells.2: none. It reads human, with present tense, uneven punctuation, the slip 'weekly few hours a week' and the self-deprecating aside about being a fifty-two-year-old woman.
tells.3: Smoothed, balanced cadence with an epiphany metaphor ending ('as if I'd discovered a room in my own house') and a 'not X so much as Y' construction.
tells.4: Evenly controlled rhythm and a neat colon-led summary line ('oddly restful: one morning a week when...').
tells.5: A forced casual insert ('humbling, sure,') and a one-line dramatic final paragraph built on 'I didn't feel triumphant. I felt...'
tells.6: Choppy 'It was somehow the kindest thing' fragment after the 'flaw' contrast was cut, plus a colon-packaged summary line.

reason: Version 2 has the rough, unpolished texture of a real writer, but its errors make it unpublishable as is. Version 4 keeps the strongest images and insight in clean, natural prose without version 5's forced casualness or version 1's over-engineered contrasts.
